title: Everyday materials
intro: What are the things around you made of? Ten questions, no pressure.

questions.prompt: Glass is made mainly by melting which common material?
questions.explanation: Most glass is made by heating sand, which is rich in silica, with a few other ingredients until it melts.

questions.prompt: Which of these metals is liquid at ordinary room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury melts at a very low temperature, so it stays liquid in a normal room. The others are solid.

questions.prompt: Most paper is made from fibres of what?
questions.explanation: Paper is a mat of fibres, usually from wood or other plants, pressed flat and dried.

questions.prompt: Which of these lets electricity flow through it most easily?
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper carry electricity well. That is why wires are metal inside and covered in plastic outside.

questions.prompt: Traditional bricks are made by baking which material?
questions.explanation: Shaped clay is dried and fired until it is hard and strong.

questions.prompt: Steel is mostly iron with a small amount of which other element?
questions.explanation: A little carbon makes iron much stronger, and the result is steel.

questions.prompt: Which of these floats on water?
questions.explanation: Cork is full of tiny air pockets, so it is less dense than water and floats.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a natural fibre?
questions.explanation: Cotton grows on a plant. Nylon, polyester and acrylic are made in factories.

questions.prompt: A material that lets light pass straight through, so you can see clearly through it, is called what?
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent. Opaque things block light, and translucent things let some through but scatter it.

questions.prompt: Why does ice float in a glass of water?
choices: It is less dense than the liquid water
questions.explanation: Water expands a little as it freezes, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.
